claims.text: High strain rate combined with moderate-to-elevated temperature causes dynamic grain refinement below a critical size in an initially single-phase high-entropy alloy.
Dynamic grain refinement below a critical size causes brittle behavior.
Extreme grain refinement suppresses dislocation-mediated plasticity and shifts deformation toward grain-boundary-dominated processes.
Grain-boundary-dominated deformation promotes localized decohesion or cavitation along high-angle grain boundaries.
High-angle grain-boundary decohesion can occur in a high-entropy solid solution without significant impurity segregation.
The initial alloy has a coarse or moderately sized grain structure, as is typical of additive manufacturing.
The initial alloy has negligible grain-boundary segregation.
Controlled deformation at high strain rate and 400–800°C promotes severe plastic deformation and dynamic grain refinement.
Dynamic deformation produces a nanograined structure at grain boundaries.
Dynamic deformation may produce a locally amorphous structure at grain boundaries.
The refined structure undergoes inverse Hall–Petch softening at high strain rate and moderate temperature.
Single-phase FCC high- and medium-entropy alloys can exhibit rapid ductility loss at 400–800°C.
At intermediate temperatures, failure can occur shortly after maximum tensile stress is reached.
Under the high-rate, intermediate-temperature condition, fracture initiates along dynamically refined grain boundaries and shows increased brittle-decohesion signatures.
At lower strain rate or lower temperature, a coarser grain structure is retained and dislocation-mediated plasticity provides higher ductility and toughness.
The proposed brittle behavior is confined to a service window in which refinement reaches a critical nanometer-scale size without oxidation or phase transformation becoming dominant.
The critical grain size and temperature/strain-rate thresholds depend on alloy composition and processing history.
If substantial refinement is achieved but intergranular brittle failure does not occur and ductility remains equivalent to baseline, the proposed mechanism is falsified.
